question:
A 53-year-old man who developed a left lower-extremity deep-vein thrombosis after hip replacement
surgery 6 months ago presents for follow-up. He has done well on apixaban, with no bleeding
complications, and has resumed normal activities with no residual leg swelling or pain. Physical
examination is entirely normal. One week ago, the patient had a repeat ultrasound of the left leg veins
as part of a research study. The ultrasound revealed a residual nonocclusive thrombus in his left
common femoral vein. Which one of the following management approaches is most appropriate for this
patient? Answer Choices: (A) Switch to prophylactic dose of apixaban (B) Place IVC filter and
discontinue anticoagulation (C) Continue apixaban for another 6 months (D) Switch to rivaroxaban (E)
Switch to warfarin therapy (F) Increase apixaban dose and continue indefinitely (G) Discontinue
apixaban (H) Continue apixaban and repeat ultrasound examination in 3 months (I) Continue apixaban
indefinitely (J) Continue apixaban and obtain CT venogram
 A. Switch to rivaroxaban
B. Switch to prophylactic dose of apixaban
C. Continue apixaban for another 6 months
D. Discontinue apixaban
E. Switch to warfarin therapy
F. Continue apixaban and repeat ultrasound examination in 3 months
G. Increase apixaban dose and continue indefinitely

H. Continue apixaban and obtain CT venogram
I. Continue apixaban indefinitely
J. Place IVC filter and discontinue anticoagulation
